chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

He was asked about a man who has only one garment, and salat is not permissible in it, and he cannot find water to wash it—what should he do? He said: “He performs tayammum and prays; then when he obtains water, he washes it and repeats the salat.”
As for the report of ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar in particular, it is possible that the blood which was on the garment was fish blood, because that is among what salat is permissible in, whether little or much.
If a person has two garments, and one of them is affected by a najāsah in which salat is not permissible, then he should pray in each one of them. That is indicated by what he narrated:
Saʿd, from ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:

I wrote to him asking about a man who had two garments, and urine affected one of them, but he did not know which one it was. The time for salat arrived, and he feared it would pass, and he had no water—what should he do? He said: “He prays in both of them together [i.e., one after the other in both garments].”
Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: It is disliked for a person to pray while there is in front of his qiblah a fire, an unsheathed weapon, an image, or something from the impurities.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the obligatory ritual prayer being discussed in legal terms
key_terms.بَوْلٌ: urine, a source of najāsah affecting the garment
key_terms.ثَوْبَانِ: two garments between which impurity is uncertain
key_terms.نَجَاسَةٌ: ritual impurity that prevents the validity of prayer in a garment
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمُ: he performs tayammum when water is unavailable
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: it is disliked, indicating karāhah rather than prohibition

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if his clothing is impure and he has no water before salat?
ai.summary: This passage discusses rulings of salat in garments affected by najāsah when water is unavailable. It explains that one with only a contaminated garment performs tayammum and prays, then washes the garment and repeats the salat upon finding water; and when one of two garments is impure but unidentified, he prays in both. It also mentions disliked matters in the direction of the qiblah during salat.
